_doc: Curated golden-query set for the rosetta retrieval surfaces. See src/eval/retrieval.ts for the runner. Each entry asserts what an agent SHOULD see when it asks this question. `expected_rosetta_ids` lists page rosetta-ids (see src/rosetta-id.ts) that are acceptable as a 'correct' top-N hit (any match counts) — NOT the numeric `pages.id`, which is a fresh rowid re-minted on every extract-docusaurus.ts run and is not a stable identity. `expected_classified` asserts the regex classifier's detection. SURFACES (`surface` field, default 'search'): 'search' exercises routeros_search/searchAll — the entry point most exposed to the Confluence→Docusaurus corpus swap — and carries the durable recall/MRR/classifier GATE (V-retrieval-floor). 'property'/'changelog'/'video' dispatch to the dedicated tools (lookupProperty/searchChangelogs/searchVideos) and feed a SEPARATE informational `surface_matrix` (per-surface hit@5) kept out of the search aggregates so those stay sensitive; surface regressions warn (per-query 'was passing, now misses') and are triaged into the Bug Ledger, not auto-gated — this is a starting coverage board to grow over time (issue #53). Keep this set small and high-signal. Add entries when you fix (or want to pin) a real behavior, not speculatively. Queries that legitimately fail today (e.g. #26 ranking regressions, or the firewall-filter property-link gap BL-1) stay pointed at the CORRECT answer and fail loudly — never loosen a fixture to make the board green.

_thresholds._doc: Absolute floors on the SEARCH-surface aggregate only (27 search queries as of #53; property/changelog/video are tracked in surface_matrix, not here). Floors are set with ~1-query headroom above observed current-corpus metrics (recall@5 92.6%, recall@3 92.6%, mrr 88.3%, classifier 100%) so they tolerate the 2 known-failing #26 ranking queries plus a little noise, and catch a systemic collapse. The TIGHT forward guard is the 2pp per-metric regression check in retrieval.ts vs baseline.json — that is what catches any single new miss (a 3rd search failure drops recall@5 ~3.7pp and trips it). Over 24 queries a '2-failure tolerance' meant recall@5≈0.92; recomputed for 27 search queries these floors keep that same 2-to-3-failure spirit rather than the pre-#53 0.85/0.70/0.65, which had drifted loose (would have tolerated 4 failures).
